description: New workspace data is stored in the app data folder (per-workspace subdirectory) before Save Workspace is triggered
steps: Open Crystal Studio and open or create a new workspace

Verify that the four session artifacts (selected target profile id, base file snapshots, parser metadata JSON, current HLR intermediate JSON) are written to the app data folder under a subdirectory keyed to the workspace path
Confirm that no .crystal-studio/ folder exists in the workspace root

description: Auto-save runs periodically and writes all four artifacts to the currently active storage target
steps: Open a workspace in pre-Save-Workspace state (data lives in app data folder)
Wait for the auto-save interval to elapse
Verify that selected target profile id, base file snapshots, parser metadata JSON, and current HLR intermediate JSON are written to the app data folder
Trigger Save Workspace from the UI
Wait for the auto-save interval to elapse again
Verify that the same four artifacts are now written to .crystal-studio/ in the workspace root instead of app data

description: Triggering Save Workspace migrates project data from app data to .crystal-studio/ in the workspace root
steps: Open a workspace with project data persisted in app data folder
Trigger Save Workspace from the UI
Verify that a .crystal-studio/ folder is created in the workspace root
Verify that all four session artifacts are present and correct inside .crystal-studio/
Verify that the app-data per-workspace subdirectory is deleted after successful migration

description: The first patch or build triggers the same data migration as an explicit Save Workspace
steps: Open a workspace in pre-Save-Workspace state (data in app data)
Trigger a patch or build without explicitly clicking Save Workspace
Verify that .crystal-studio/ is created in the workspace root
Verify that all four session artifacts are migrated from app data to .crystal-studio/
Verify that the app-data per-workspace subdirectory is removed after migration

description: .crystal-studio/ is added to .gitignore when the folder is first created
steps: Open a workspace whose root already contains a .gitignore file
Trigger Save Workspace
Open .gitignore and verify that .crystal-studio/ appears as an entry
Repeat the test with a workspace that has no .gitignore; verify the file is created containing .crystal-studio/

description: Once .crystal-studio/ exists it becomes the sole auto-save target; app data folder is never written to again
steps: Open a workspace that already has a .crystal-studio/ folder
Perform an HLR edit to mark the session as dirty
Wait for the auto-save interval to elapse
Verify that updated artifacts are written to .crystal-studio/ only
Verify that no new write occurred in the app data folder for this workspace

description: On startup, the session is restored from .crystal-studio/ when that folder exists
steps: Open a workspace that has a .crystal-studio/ folder containing all four saved artifacts
Restart Crystal Studio
Verify that the project config and selected target profile id are loaded from .crystal-studio/
Verify that the HLR is reconstructed by the HLR factory from the saved intermediate JSON (not by re-parsing ASM files from disk)
Verify that no re-parse dialog appears if no parsed file has changed on disk

description: On startup, the session is restored from the app data folder when .crystal-studio/ does not exist
steps: Open a workspace that has no .crystal-studio/ folder but has artifacts stored in app data
Restart Crystal Studio
Verify that the project config and selected target profile id are loaded from the app data folder
Verify that the HLR is reconstructed from the saved intermediate JSON in app data

description: User is prompted to re-parse when a previously parsed ASM file has changed on disk since the last snapshot
steps: Open a workspace and let Crystal Studio restore its session normally
Using an external editor, modify an ASM file that was captured in the last base file snapshot
Restart Crystal Studio
Verify that a dialog appears informing the user that a parsed file has changed on disk, offering Re-parse or Keep HLR
Choose Re-parse and verify the HLR is rebuilt from the current disk content
Repeat the scenario, choose Keep HLR, and verify the session HLR is unchanged and the on-disk modification is effectively ignored

description: Stale project entries are flagged on startup when the associated workspace path no longer exists on disk
steps: Register a project by opening a workspace at a specific path
Delete or rename the workspace directory on disk while Crystal Studio is closed
Start Crystal Studio
Verify that the stale project entry is shown in the project list with a warning indicator
Verify that an action is offered to delete the stale entry

description: User can manually forget a project from the UI; the action removes the entry from the list
steps: Open Crystal Studio with at least one project registered in the project list
Trigger the Forget / Remove action on a chosen project entry
Verify that the project entry disappears from the list
Verify that the .crystal-studio/ folder (or app data artifacts) for that project are NOT automatically deleted from disk — the user owns those files

description: SessionService is instantiated in the service container and its IPC channels are registered and reachable from the renderer
steps: Inspect serviceContainer.ts and confirm a SessionService instance is created and included in the ServiceContainer type
Inspect registerIpc.ts and confirm that the session-related IPC channels (save workspace, get session state) are registered
Invoke the save-workspace IPC channel from the renderer and verify that the migration from app data to .crystal-studio/ is triggered
Invoke the auto-save channel and confirm that the correct set of four artifacts is written to the active storage target

description: Auto-save writes are atomic: a crash or forced kill during a save does not leave partially-written or corrupted artifact files
steps: Simulate a crash mid-write using a mock that interrupts the I/O operation after the first artifact is written
Restart Crystal Studio
Verify that the last fully committed artifact set loads intact
Verify that no partially-written artifact files are present in the save directory

description: App data folder artifacts are deleted only after .crystal-studio/ artifacts have been fully and successfully written
steps: Trigger Save Workspace in a workspace where app data artifacts exist
Simulate a failure mid-migration (e.g. disk full or permission error when writing .crystal-studio/)
Verify that the app data folder artifacts are still intact and have not been deleted
Verify that Crystal Studio can still restore the session from app data on the next startup
